topic.name: General Solutions of Trigonometric Equations With Transformed Functions

question.text:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

\[ \cos\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \]

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as \[ x = a^\circ + n \cdot 240^\circ, \qquad x = 210^\circ + n\cdot 240^\circ, \] where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
The general solution to our equation is

\begin{align*} \dfrac{3x}{2} &= 45^\circ + n\cdot 360^\circ,&\qquad&\qquad& \dfrac{3x}{2} &= 315^\circ + n\cdot 360^\circ . \end{align*}

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

\begin{align*} 3x &=90^\circ + n\cdot 720^\circ &\qquad&\qquad& 3x &= 630^\circ+ n\cdot 720^\circ\\[5pt] x&= 30^\circ + n\cdot 240^\circ &\qquad&\qquad& x &= 210^\circ + n\cdot 240^\circ \end{align*}

Therefore, $a=30.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Cosine Function

question.text:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: \[ \cos \left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) = 1 \]

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as \[ x = a\pi + \pi n, \] where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[-1,0).$
question.explanation:
The general solution to our equation is \begin{align*} 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} &= 0 + 2\pi n. \end{align*}

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get \begin{align*} 2x &= -\dfrac{\pi}{3}+ 2\pi n\\[5pt] x &= -\dfrac{\pi}{6}+ \pi n. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have that $a= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{1}{6}}.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Cosine Function

question.text:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: \[ \tan{\left(5x + 75^\circ \right)} = -1 \]

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as \[ x = a^\circ + n\cdot 36^\circ, \] where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value $a$ in the range $[0^\circ, 36^\circ).$
question.explanation:
The general solution to our equation is

\begin{align*} 5x + 75^\circ &= 135^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ. \end{align*}

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get \begin{align*} 5x &= 135^\circ - 75^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ\\[5pt] 5x &= 60^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ \\[5pt] x &= 12^\circ + n \cdot 36^\circ. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have that $a=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{12}.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 
\[
\cot\left( \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) = -1
\]
The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 
\[
x = a\pi + 2n\pi,
\]
where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $\left[0,2\right).$
question.explanation:
The given equation is equivalent to \[ \tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) = -1. \]

So, the general solution to our equation is \begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} &= -\dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi. \end{align*}

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{2} &= \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi \\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{2} &= \dfrac{\pi}{12} + n\pi \\[5pt] x & = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have that $a = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{6}}.$

example.title: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function

question.text:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: \[ \csc\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \]

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as \[ x = a\pi + 4\pi n , \qquad x = -\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + 4\pi n, \] where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $(-4, 0].$
question.explanation:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to \[ \sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}. \]

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is \[ \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 2\pi n, \qquad \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = -\dfrac{\pi}{3} + 2\pi n . \]

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get \begin{align} \dfrac{x}{2} & = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2\pi n, & \qquad & \dfrac{x}{2} = -\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2\pi n \\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{2} & = -\dfrac{11\pi}{12} + 2\pi n, & \qquad & \dfrac{x}{2} = -\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + 2\pi n \\[5pt] x & = -\dfrac{11\pi}{6} + 4\pi n, & \qquad & x = -\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + 4\pi n. \end{align}

So, we have that $a = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{11}{6}}.$
